# Swarm networking surface area

Scope: Swarm networking: the configuration of the cluster and its nodes, Swarm-scoped networks, the
overlay network driver's options and networks, and the ingress network, as observable from outside
the daemon.

This document is a behavior specification. For how the parts work, see [design.md](../../../daemon/libnetwork/docs/design.md), [network.md](../../../daemon/libnetwork/docs/network.md) and [networkdb.md](../../../daemon/libnetwork/docs/networkdb.md).

[../README.md](../README.md) gives the model that this spec follows: the items of a spec, their
categories and what their verdicts depend on. [README.md](README.md) gives the conventions of the
networking specs, such as vantage points, daemon settings, timing and convergence ceilings, and host
requirements. The other specs in this directory use the same conventions. Unless an expectation says
otherwise, a `ctr` in this document is a standalone container attached to an `attachable`
overlay.

In this spec, an overlay network is an overlay network other than the ingress network, unless an
expectation includes the ingress network. A node has a local attachment to a network while a task, a
standalone container or the node's load-balancer endpoint on that network is on the node. A network
is programmed on a node while the node has a local attachment to it. A node creates its
load-balancer endpoint on a network with the network, and deletes it with the network. Except on the
ingress network, the node deletes the network once no task or standalone container of the node is on
it, so the load-balancer endpoint does not outlast them. Unless an expectation or its section names
other values, an expectation holds in a Swarm with the cluster settings that `POST
/swarm/init` sets by default. An expectation holds whatever data-path, advertise and listen
addresses each node gives in `POST /swarm/init` or `POST /swarm/join`, when the
data-path addresses of the Swarm's nodes are all of one IP version, and when each node's route for
its VXLAN traffic to the other nodes selects its data-path address as the source address
([Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals)), unless the expectation names that case.

An expectation that involves the ingress network holds for an ingress network that was created with
`Ingress` set, that is not `internal` and that does not have the option `dsr`.
Only an expectation that names an ingress network without `Ingress` covers such a network
([The ingress network](#swarm-networking-the-ingress-network)). An expectation that involves a node's gateway network
holds for one that the daemon created, or that the operator created with the options of one that the
daemon creates and no others but a subnet and a gateway ([Gateway network](swarm-traffic.md#swarm-traffic-gateway-network)),
unless the expectation names other options. The daemon creates its gateway network with
`com.docker.network.bridge.name` set to `docker_gwbridge`,
`com.docker.network.bridge.enable_icc` set to `false` and
`com.docker.network.bridge.enable_ip_masquerade` set to `true`. On an overlay network with
more than one subnet, an expectation about traffic to a VIP holds for the VIP and a backend task
only when both are in the subnet of the load-balancer endpoint of the client's node on that network
([Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals)). On Linux nodes, an expectation about a
`mode=host` published port holds for a service that is attached to at least one network
that is not `internal`, and for a service whose spec names no network and that publishes no port
in ingress mode, since its tasks run on the default bridge network
([Egress & the gateway network](swarm-traffic.md#swarm-traffic-egress-the-gateway-network)). An expectation about reaching a
`mode=host` published port at an address of the node holds on a network whose gateway
mode for that address's family is not `routed`, without
`com.docker.network.bridge.host_binding_ipv4` and
`com.docker.network.bridge.inhibit_ipv4`, unless the expectation names them
([bridge-networking.md](bridge-networking.md)).

<a id="swarm-networking-rationales"></a>

## Rationales

<a id="RAT-SWARM-PREDEFINED-NETWORKS"></a>

**Rationale RAT-SWARM-PREDEFINED-NETWORKS**: The Swarm's bridge and host networks stand for each node's own network

*Rationale of:* [NET-API-INSPECT-NAME-SWARM-PREDEFINED](network-common.md#NET-API-INSPECT-NAME-SWARM-PREDEFINED), [SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-NOT-LISTED](#SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-NOT-LISTED)

A service that names `bridge` or `host` stores the ID of one of the Swarm's
predefined networks, and `GET /services/{id}` and `GET /tasks` report that
ID. The task's container uses the node's own network of that name. The network list leaves the
Swarm's predefined networks out, so that it shows each of `bridge` and
`host` once, as the network that containers use. A lookup by ID finds them, so that
the IDs in services and tasks resolve to a network. A lookup by the name `bridge` or
`host` without `scope` `swarm` finds the node's own network, which is
what the name means on every node. Listing them would show two networks of each name on every
manager to the tooling that reads the list. A lookup by name that matched them would make the
names `bridge` and `host` ambiguous on every manager, and a lookup by ID that
did not find them would leave those IDs without a network. Each of these changes should be made
on purpose.

<a id="swarm-networking-host-requirements"></a>

## Host requirements

The conventions for this section are in [README.md](README.md#readme-host-requirements). The kernel
facilities and programs are requirements of each Linux node. The Windows facilities are requirements
of each Windows node.

*Facility:* **iptables**, accepting the filter, mangle and nat tables, the
`MARK`, `DNAT`, `SNAT` and `REDIRECT` targets,
and the `ipvs`, `conntrack`, `sctp`, `bpf`, `policy`, `owner` and `mark` matches

*Needed when:* Always

<a id="SWARM-HOST-IP6TABLES-COMMAND"></a>

**Host requirement SWARM-HOST-IP6TABLES-COMMAND**: ip6tables with the tables, targets and matches it needs

*Platforms:* linux · *When:* iptables-backend · *Kind:* program · *Tags:* encrypted, ipv6

*Needed by:* [SWARM-CTR-MTU-ENCRYPTED-V6](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-MTU-ENCRYPTED-V6)

*Facility:* **ip6tables**, accepting the filter and mangle tables, the `MARK`
target, and the `bpf`, `policy`, `owner` and `mark` matches

*Needed when:* The iptables backend, and an `encrypted` overlay network on a node with
an IPv6 data-path address

The daemon does not depend on which implementation of **iptables** and **ip6tables**
the host has. The kernel options that the programs need depend on that implementation:

<a id="SWARM-HOST-IP6TABLES-KERNEL"></a>

**Host requirement SWARM-HOST-IP6TABLES-KERNEL**: Kernel options for ip6tables

*Platforms:* linux · *When:* iptables-backend · *Kind:* os · *Kernel options:* `NETFILTER`, `NETFILTER_ADVANCED`, `NETFILTER_XTABLES`, `NF_CONNTRACK`, `NF_NAT`, `NETFILTER_XT_MARK`, `NETFILTER_XT_NAT`, `NETFILTER_XT_TARGET_REDIRECT`, `NETFILTER_XT_MATCH_IPVS`, `NETFILTER_XT_MATCH_CONNTRACK`, `NETFILTER_XT_MATCH_SCTP`, `NETFILTER_XT_MATCH_BPF`, `NETFILTER_XT_MATCH_POLICY`, `NETFILTER_XT_MATCH_OWNER`

The kernel options that **ip6tables** needs, whichever implementation provides it.
*Kernel options:* The options that iptables needs, whichever implementation provides it

<a id="SWARM-HOST-IP6TABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL"></a>

**Host requirement SWARM-HOST-IP6TABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL**: Kernel options for ip6tables from iptables-legacy

*Platforms:* linux · *When:* iptables-backend, iptables-legacy · *Kind:* os · *Kernel options:* `IP6_NF_IPTABLES`, `IP6_NF_FILTER`, `IP6_NF_MANGLE`, `IP6_NF_IPTABLES_LEGACY`, `NETFILTER_XTABLES_LEGACY`

The kernel options that **ip6tables** needs when iptables-legacy provides it. *Kernel
options:* `IP6_NF_IPTABLES`, `IP6_NF_FILTER`, `IP6_NF_MANGLE`.
`IP6_NF_IPTABLES_LEGACY` from Linux 6.9, and `NETFILTER_XTABLES_LEGACY` from
Linux 6.17.

<a id="SWARM-HOST-IP6TABLES-NFT-KERNEL"></a>

**Host requirement SWARM-HOST-IP6TABLES-NFT-KERNEL**: Kernel options for ip6tables from iptables-nft

*Platforms:* linux · *When:* iptables-backend, iptables-nft · *Kind:* os · *Kernel options:* `NF_TABLES`, `NF_TABLES_IPV6`, `NFT_COMPAT`, `NFT_CHAIN_ROUTE_IPV6`

The kernel options that **ip6tables** needs when iptables-nft provides it. *Kernel
options:* `NF_TABLES`, `NF_TABLES_IPV6`, `NFT_COMPAT`. Before Linux
5.2, `NFT_CHAIN_ROUTE_IPV6` for the `OUTPUT` chain of the mangle table.

<a id="swarm-networking-interop-premise"></a>

## Interop premise

Wire and protocol compatibility is a hard requirement. Users upgrade a Swarm node by node. During a
rollout, the cluster is heterogeneous. Nodes with different engine versions must share an overlay
network and an ingress network. Everything in [Wire format & interop](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-wire-format-interop) is
contract.

<a id="swarm-networking-cluster-node-configuration"></a>

## Cluster & node configuration

These expectations cover cluster configuration. The accepted range of the data-path port is 1024 to
49151. The reference for `docker swarm init --data-path-port` documents this range.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS**: DataPathAddr sets the address peers send the node's VXLAN traffic to

*Observed from:* underlay (outer destination address) · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

`DataPathAddr` in `POST /swarm/init` or `POST /swarm/join` sets the
address peers send the node's VXLAN traffic to.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-DEFAULT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-DEFAULT**: Without DataPathAddr, peers send VXLAN traffic to the advertise address

*Observed from:* underlay (outer destination address) · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Without `DataPathAddr`, peers send the node's VXLAN traffic to its advertise address.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-IFACE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS-IFACE**: Peers keep sending to the address a DataPathAddr interface first had

*Observed from:* underlay (outer destination address) · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

`DataPathAddr` in `POST /swarm/init` or `POST /swarm/join` names a
network interface. Peers then send the node's VXLAN traffic to the address that the interface
had when the request was made. They continue to send it to that address after the interface's
address changes, and after the daemon restarts. See
[Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-ADDRESS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-ADDRESS**: VXLAN traffic's outer source address is the one the route selects

*Observed from:* underlay (outer source address) · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

A node's VXLAN traffic to a peer has the outer source address that the node's route to that peer
selects. This holds whether or not that address is the node's data-path address. See
[Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT**: DataPathPort in POST /swarm/init sets the cluster's VXLAN UDP port

*Observed from:* underlay · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

`DataPathPort` in `POST /swarm/init` sets the VXLAN UDP port for the whole
cluster. See [Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-DEFAULT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-DEFAULT**: Linux and Windows nodes exchange overlay traffic on the default port

*Observed from:* task · *Depends on:* os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A Swarm with the default data-path port

Linux and Windows nodes in that Swarm exchange overlay traffic. The default data-path port is
the UDP port that Windows nodes always use for VXLAN.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID-CLI**: docker swarm init refuses a data-path port outside the accepted range

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form of:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A node that is not yet in a Swarm

`docker swarm init` with a data-path port outside the accepted range exits non-zero. The
node is then still not in a Swarm.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID**: POST /swarm/init refuses a data-path port outside the accepted range

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID-CLI](#SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A node that is not yet in a Swarm

`POST /swarm/init` with a data-path port outside the accepted range responds with a 4xx
or 5xx status. The node is then still not in a Swarm.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID-HTTP500"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-INVALID-HTTP500**: A data-path port outside the accepted range responds 500

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A node that is not yet in a Swarm

`POST /swarm/init` with a data-path port outside the accepted range responds 500. See
[Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-ZERO"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-PORT-ZERO**: A data-path port of 0 in POST /swarm/init selects 4789

*Observed from:* api:solo, api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A node that is not yet in a Swarm

`POST /swarm/init` with a data-path port of 0 responds 200. `GET /info` on the
node then reports 4789 as the data-path port in `Swarm.Cluster`.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOL-ALLOCATION"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-ADDRESS-POOL-ALLOCATION**: An overlay without a subnet gets one of SubnetSize from DefaultAddrPool

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* An overlay network, the ingress network included, that uses the default IPAM
driver and is created without a subnet

Once the network is allocated ([Network lifecycle & API surface](#swarm-networking-network-lifecycle-api-surface)),
`GET /networks/{id}` on a manager reports a subnet for it. That subnet is inside one of
the `DefaultAddrPool` prefixes that `GET /info` on a manager reports in
`Swarm.Cluster`. The prefix length of that subnet is the `SubnetSize` that
`GET /info` reports.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID-CLI**: docker swarm init refuses a mask length over 29 or below a pool's prefix

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form of:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID](#SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A node that is not yet in a Swarm

`docker swarm init` with `--default-addr-pool` exits non-zero when
`--default-addr-pool-mask-length` is greater than 29. It also exits non-zero when that
mask length is less than the prefix length of one of the pools. In both cases, the node is then
still not in a Swarm.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID**: POST /swarm/init refuses a SubnetSize over 29 or below a pool's prefix

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID-CLI](#SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A node that is not yet in a Swarm

`POST /swarm/init` with `DefaultAddrPool` set responds with a 4xx or 5xx
status when the request's `SubnetSize` is greater than 29. It also responds with a
4xx or 5xx status when the request's `SubnetSize` is less than the prefix length of one of the pools, or is 0 and one of the pools has a prefix longer than 24 bits. In both cases, the node is then still not in a Swarm.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID-HTTP500"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-INVALID-HTTP500**: A SubnetSize over 29 or below a pool's prefix responds 500

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A node that is not yet in a Swarm

`POST /swarm/init` with `DefaultAddrPool` set responds 500 when the request's
`SubnetSize` is greater than 29. It also responds 500 when the request's
`SubnetSize` is less than the prefix length of one of the pools, or is 0 and one of the pools has a prefix longer than 24 bits. See
[Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-ZERO"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-ZERO**: POST /swarm/init accepts a SubnetSize of 0, and GET /info reports 0

*Observed from:* api:solo, api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A node that is not yet in a Swarm

`POST /swarm/init` with `DefaultAddrPool` set, with no prefix longer than 24 bits, and a `SubnetSize` of 0 responds 200. `GET /info` on the node then reports a `SubnetSize` of 0
in `Swarm.Cluster`. See [Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER**: A manager's GET /info reports the data-path port, pool and subnet size

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form:* [SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER-CLI](#SWARM-CLUSTER-INFO-MANAGER-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

On a manager, `GET /info` includes `Swarm.Cluster`.

whatever `SubnetSize` the request gave.

<a id="swarm-networking-network-lifecycle-api-surface"></a>

## Network lifecycle & API surface

A Swarm-scoped network is a network that the Swarm managers keep. Its driver is a multi-host driver,
such as `overlay`, or a node-local driver, such as `bridge`. A network of a
node-local driver is Swarm-scoped when it is created with `Scope` set to `swarm`
(`--scope swarm`).

A Swarm-scoped network is allocated after the network is created, and asynchronously. In this spec,
a network is allocated once `GET /networks/{id}` on a manager reports the network's
`Driver`.

<a id="swarm-networking-overlay-driver-options"></a>

### Overlay driver options

An expectation in this section that refers to other expectations or to another section covers only
whether the daemon accepts and honors the option. Its `depends_on` field also covers only that.
The expectations or the section that it refers to specify the behavior that the option selects, and
what that behavior depends on.

<a id="SWARM-OVLOPT-MTU"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVLOPT-MTU**: The mtu option sets the base MTU before encapsulation overhead

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows · *Key:* `com.docker.network.driver.mtu`

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Sets the base MTU from which encapsulation overhead is subtracted. See
[*SWARM-CTR-MTU-CLEARTEXT*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-MTU-CLEARTEXT), [*SWARM-CTR-MTU-CLEARTEXT-V6*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-MTU-CLEARTEXT-V6),
[*SWARM-CTR-MTU-ENCRYPTED*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-MTU-ENCRYPTED) and [*SWARM-CTR-MTU-ENCRYPTED-V6*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-CTR-MTU-ENCRYPTED-V6).

<a id="SWARM-OVLOPT-VNI-LIST"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVLOPT-VNI-LIST**: The vxlanid_list option sets one VNI per IPAM subnet

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows · *Key:* `com.docker.network.driver.overlay.vxlanid_list`

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Sets the VNIs, one per IPAM subnet. See [*SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST*](#SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST).

<a id="SWARM-OVLOPT-ENCRYPTED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVLOPT-ENCRYPTED**: The encrypted option selects an encrypted overlay

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows · *Key:* `encrypted`

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN), [SWARM-HOST-XFRM](#SWARM-HOST-XFRM)

Selects an encrypted overlay. See [Encryption](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-encryption).

<a id="SWARM-OVLOPT-DSR"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVLOPT-DSR**: The dsr option selects direct server return for east-west VIP traffic

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows · *Key:* `dsr`

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPVS](#SWARM-HOST-IPVS), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Selects direct server return for east-west VIP traffic on Linux nodes. See
[*SWARM-LB-DSR-SOURCE*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-LB-DSR-SOURCE) and [*SWARM-LB-DSR-DESTINATION*](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-LB-DSR-DESTINATION).

<a id="SWARM-OVLOPT-FLAG-ANY-VALUE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVLOPT-FLAG-ANY-VALUE**: On Linux, encrypted and dsr take effect whatever their value

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows · *Key:* `encrypted`, `dsr`

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPVS](#SWARM-HOST-IPVS), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN), [SWARM-HOST-XFRM](#SWARM-HOST-XFRM)

On Linux nodes, each key takes effect when it is present in the network's options, whatever its
value. This includes the empty string and `false` as values.

<a id="swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks"></a>

### Swarm-scoped networks

The expectations in this subsection hold for any Swarm-scoped network, whatever its driver.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE**: A manager creates a network with Scope swarm or a multi-host driver

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A manager, and a network driver that is built in or that a managed plugin provides

On that manager, `POST /networks/create` with a name that no Swarm-scoped network has,
and no network on that manager has, responds 201 when it sets `Scope` to `swarm` or
names a multi-host driver, such as `overlay`. `GET /networks` on a manager then
lists the network.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-CLI**: docker network create --scope=swarm or --driver overlay makes a network

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form of:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE](#SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A manager

On that manager, `docker network create --scope=swarm` with a name that no Swarm-scoped
network has, and no network on that manager has, exits zero. `docker network create
--driver overlay` with such a name, in place of the first command, also exits zero. `docker
network ls` on a manager then lists the network.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-ALLOCATED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-ALLOCATED**: A Swarm-scoped network reports its Driver within the allocation ceiling

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION)

Within the [*allocation ceiling (30 s)*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION) after
`POST /networks/create` for a Swarm-scoped network responds 201, `GET
/networks/{id}` on a manager reports the network's `Driver`. This does not apply to a
network that cannot be allocated ([*SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-INSPECT*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-SCALE-UNALLOCATABLE-INSPECT)).

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-WORKER-HTTP403"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-WORKER-HTTP403**: Creating a Swarm-scoped network on a worker responds 403

*Observed from:* api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-WORKER-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-WORKER-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

On a worker, `POST /networks/create` with `Scope` set to `swarm` responds 403. It also
responds 403 with a multi-host driver, such as `overlay`, whatever `Scope` the request
gives.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-WORKER-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-WORKER-CLI**: docker network create of a Swarm-scoped network fails on a worker

*Observed from:* api:wkr · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form of:* [SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-WORKER-HTTP403](#SWARM-SCOPED-CREATE-WORKER-HTTP403) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

On a worker, `docker network create --scope=swarm` exits non-zero and prints the daemon's
error. `docker network create --driver overlay` also exits non-zero and prints the daemon's
error. See [Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-SERVICE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-SERVICE**: A network that a service references is not deleted

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form:* [SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-SERVICE-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-SERVICE-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A Swarm with a Swarm-scoped network other than the ingress network
([The ingress network](#swarm-networking-the-ingress-network)), and a service that references the network

`DELETE /networks/{id}` for the network responds with a 4xx or 5xx status. The network
stays listed.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-SERVICE-HTTP400"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-SERVICE-HTTP400**: Deleting a network that a service references responds 400

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A Swarm with a Swarm-scoped network other than the ingress network
([The ingress network](#swarm-networking-the-ingress-network)), and a service that references the network

`DELETE /networks/{id}` for the network responds 400, with a message that contains
`is in use by service`. See [Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK**: A network with an attached task or container is not deleted

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form:* [SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A Swarm with a Swarm-scoped network other than the ingress network
([The ingress network](#swarm-networking-the-ingress-network)), and a task or container attached to it that is
not shutting down

`DELETE /networks/{id}` for the network responds with a 4xx or 5xx status. The network
stays listed.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK-HTTP400"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-DELETE-IN-USE-TASK-HTTP400**: Deleting a network with an attached task or container responds 400

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A Swarm with a Swarm-scoped network other than the ingress network
([The ingress network](#swarm-networking-the-ingress-network)), and a task or container attached to it that is
not shutting down

`DELETE /networks/{id}` for the network responds 400, with a message that contains

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-CONFLICT"></a>

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

reports the `Driver`, `Ingress`, `Attachable`,

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-DANGLING"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-DANGLING**: dangling=true lists every Swarm-scoped network, and false attached ones

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Concerned by:* [NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-SWARM-SCOPED](network-common.md#NET-API-FILTER-DANGLING-SWARM-SCOPED)

*Applies to:* A manager

`GET /networks` with the filter `dangling=true` lists every Swarm-scoped
network, including the ingress network and networks that services use. `GET /networks`

attachment on that manager. Those networks are then in both responses. See
[Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A manager that does not have a local attachment to an overlay network

On that manager, `GET /networks/{id}` for that network responds 200. The response
reports the `IPAM` of the network's allocation and an empty `Containers`.
It does not include `Peers`.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-MANAGER-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-LIST-MANAGER-CLI**: docker network ls on a manager lists each Swarm-scoped network

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

`docker network ls` on a manager lists each Swarm-scoped network.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-NOT-LISTED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-PREDEFINED-NOT-LISTED**: On a manager, GET /networks never lists the Swarm's bridge or host network

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Rationale:* The Swarm's bridge and host networks stand for each node's own network ([RAT-SWARM-PREDEFINED-NETWORKS](#RAT-SWARM-PREDEFINED-NETWORKS))

On a manager, `GET /networks` does not list the Swarm's predefined networks, with or
without filters. This includes the filters `scope=swarm`, `type=builtin`,
`type=custom` and `dangling=true`, and an `id` filter with
the full ID of one of them.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START**: A container on an attachable network starts on any active node

*Observed from:* api:active · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form:* [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

On any node whose availability is `active`, `POST /containers/{id}/start` for a
created or stopped container on an attachable Swarm-scoped network responds 204. The container
is then running and has an address on the network. For a network created with
`ConfigFrom`, this holds for a network of a node-local driver, on a node that has the
config-only network that `ConfigFrom` names.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START-CLI**: docker run on an attachable network succeeds on any active node

*Observed from:* api:active · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form of:* [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-START) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

On any node whose availability is `active`, `docker run -d --network` naming an
attachable Swarm-scoped network exits zero. The container then runs and is attached to the
network. For a network created with `ConfigFrom`, this holds for a network of a
node-local driver, on a node that has the config-only network that `ConfigFrom`
names.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT**: A running container connects to an attachable network on any active node

*Observed from:* api:active · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form:* [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

On any node whose availability is `active`, `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to an
attachable Swarm-scoped network, for a running standalone container, responds 200. The container
then has an address on the network. For a network created with `ConfigFrom`, this
holds for a network of a node-local driver, on a node that has the config-only network that
`ConfigFrom` names.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT-CLI**: docker network connect to an attachable network succeeds on active nodes

*Observed from:* api:active · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form of:* [SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT](#SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACHABLE-CONNECT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

On any node whose availability is `active`, `docker network connect` naming an attachable
Swarm-scoped network and a running standalone container exits zero. The container then has an
address on the network. For a network created with `ConfigFrom`, this holds for a

network on a manager then responds 204.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-START-HTTP500"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-DRAINED-START-HTTP500**: Starting on a drained or paused node responds 500 after 20 seconds

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A created or stopped container on an attachable Swarm-scoped network, on a node

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds 500 after 20 seconds, with a
message that contains `attaching to network failed, make sure your network options
are correct and check manager logs: context deadline exceeded`. See
[Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form:* [SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-V4-DISABLED-CLI](#SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-V4-DISABLED-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

`POST /networks/create` for a Swarm-scoped network of a node-local driver with
`EnableIPv4` false, at API version 1.48 or later, responds 400 with `IPv4

[Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-IPAM-MANAGER"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-IPAM-MANAGER**: A manager reports empty IPAM and no Options for a node-local network

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

A `POST /networks/create` request for a Swarm-scoped network of a node-local driver
without `ConfigFrom` has a subnet and gateway in `IPAM.Config`. Its
`Options` has only the driver's own options, such as
`com.docker.network.bridge.*`, or no options. The request responds 201. `GET
/networks/{id}` on a manager then reports an empty `IPAM` and does not report any
`Options`. See [Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

*Applies to:* A Swarm-scoped network of a node-local driver that was created without

allocation. See [Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-UNTAGGED-DRIVER"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-UNTAGGED-DRIVER**: A driver plugin named without its tag responds 500

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

On that manager, `POST /networks/create` for a Swarm-scoped network whose

responds 500, with a message that contains `could not resolve driver`. See
[Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

`POST /networks/create` for an overlay network whose IPAM driver is the plugin's name
without its tag responds 201. This holds whether or not the manager that handles the request has
the plugin. The network is never allocated

[Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

A service task whose network attachment requests an `ifname` that the OS refuses fails.
Its error in `GET /tasks` contains the requested name.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-IFNAME-ANY-VALUE"></a>

For any value of `ifname`, `POST /services/create` for a service whose network
attachment requests an `ifname` responds 201, and `GET /services` then lists the
service. See [Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-IFNAME-REFUSED-MSG**: A task with a refused ifname reports error renaming interface

*Applies to:* A service whose network attachment requests an `ifname` that the OS

The error of each task of the service in `GET /tasks` contains `error
renaming interface`. See [Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-HOST-NETWORK-COMBINED"></a>

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

`POST /services/create` for a service attached to the `host` network and to an
overlay network responds 201. So does a request for a service on `host` that publishes
a port in ingress mode. Each task of such a service fails. See
[Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="swarm-networking-overlay-networks"></a>

### Overlay networks

The expectations in this subsection depend on the addresses that are allocated for a network: its
subnets, task addresses and VIPs. These addresses are allocated only for an overlay network. Where
an expectation says that `GET /services/{id}` then reports a VIP, it reports it within the
allocation ceiling ([Convergence](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-convergence)) after the request responds.

<a id="SWARM-OVL-V4-DISABLED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVL-V4-DISABLED**: An overlay network with IPv4 disabled responds 400

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form:* [SWARM-OVL-V4-DISABLED-CLI](#SWARM-OVL-V4-DISABLED-CLI) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

On a manager, `POST /networks/create` for an overlay network with
`EnableIPv4` false, at API version 1.48 or later, responds 400. At any version, the
request also responds 400 when the `com.docker.network.enable_ipv4` option is set to
`false`. See [Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals).

<a id="SWARM-OVL-V4-DISABLED-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVL-V4-DISABLED-CLI**: docker network create --driver overlay fails with IPv4 disabled

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*CLI form of:* [SWARM-OVL-V4-DISABLED](#SWARM-OVL-V4-DISABLED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

On a manager, `docker network create --driver overlay --ipv4=false` exits non-zero and
prints the daemon's error. So does the same command with `--opt
com.docker.network.enable_ipv4=false` in place of `--ipv4=false`.

<a id="SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST**: A user-specified vxlanid_list gives subnet i the VNI i

*Observed from:* underlay · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

A user-specified `vxlanid_list` is honored: subnet *i* uses VNI *i*.

<a id="SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-SHORT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-SHORT**: A short vxlanid_list gets auto-allocated VNIs for the remaining subnets

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

`POST /networks/create` for an overlay network whose `vxlanid_list` has fewer
VNIs than the network has subnets responds 201. Once the network is allocated
([Network lifecycle & API surface](#swarm-networking-network-lifecycle-api-surface)), `GET /networks/{id}` on a
manager reports the same number of VNIs in `vxlanid_list` as the overlay has subnets.
These are the requested VNIs, then an auto-allocated VNI for each remaining subnet.

<a id="SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-LONG"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVL-VNI-LIST-LONG**: A long vxlanid_list keeps its first VNIs and leaves the rest free

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

`POST /networks/create` for an overlay network whose `vxlanid_list` has more
VNIs than the network has subnets responds 201. Once the network is allocated
([Network lifecycle & API surface](#swarm-networking-network-lifecycle-api-surface)), `GET /networks/{id}` on a
manager reports the same number of VNIs in `vxlanid_list` as the overlay has subnets.
These are the first VNIs of the requested list. `POST /networks/create` for another
overlay network whose `vxlanid_list` has one of the remaining VNIs responds 201, and
that network is then allocated.

<a id="SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE**: An overlay network with another overlay's VNI is created

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

`POST /networks/create` for another overlay network, with a VNI in its

<a id="SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE-CLI"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVL-VNI-DUPLICATE-CLI**: docker network create with another overlay's VNI succeeds

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* cli · *Platforms:* linux, windows

<a id="SWARM-OVL-UNALLOCATED-OTHERS-LISTED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVL-UNALLOCATED-OTHERS-LISTED**: An unallocated overlay does not hide other Swarm-scoped networks

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

An overlay network that is not allocated does not prevent `GET /networks` from listing
any other Swarm-scoped network. It also does not prevent `GET /networks/{id}` from

<a id="SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-RELEASED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVL-STATIC-ADDRESS-RELEASED**: A container's address is free for a static address once it leaves

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A standalone container on an attachable overlay

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for another container on the overlay, with the first
container's address as its static IPv4 address, then responds 204.

*Observed from:* api:mgr, api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Within the ceiling of the convergence class ([Convergence](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-convergence)) of a change to
the service's tasks, the tasks that `GET /networks/{id}?verbose=true` reports for the

<a id="SWARM-OVL-STATUS-TOTAL"></a>

On a manager, at API version 1.52 or later, `GET /networks/{id}`, with the network's
name or a partial ID, reports `IPsInUse` and `DynamicIPsAvailable` for the

<a id="SWARM-OVL-STATUS-WORKER"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVL-STATUS-WORKER**: A worker's Status.IPAM reflects only the worker's own endpoints

*Observed from:* api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

*Applies to:* A worker with a local attachment to an overlay network

At API version 1.52 or later, the `Status.IPAM` of `GET /networks/{id}` on
that worker reflects only the worker's own endpoints. It does not change when a task attaches on
another node.

A regression revealed the failed-allocation expectation. In that regression, one unallocated network
made listing and inspection fail for every Swarm-scoped network. [moby/moby#53325](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53325) fixed the regression.

The lower bound of the range of auto-allocated VNIs avoids the 802.1Q VLAN range for Windows.

<a id="swarm-networking-the-ingress-network"></a>

### The ingress network

A Swarm-scoped network created with `Ingress` set is an ingress network. An overlay
network named `ingress` and created with the label `com.docker.swarm.internal` is
also an ingress network, whatever the label's value. Older daemons created the ingress network in
this second form, without `Ingress`. `GET /networks` reports `Ingress`
as true for both forms.

An ingress network exists while `GET /networks` on a manager lists a network whose
`Ingress` is true. That network is the ingress network. `swarm init` creates it with
`Ingress` set and names it `ingress`. It can be removed, and an ingress network
can then be created with another name. A copy that a node keeps after the network is deleted
([Known divergences & non-goals](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-known-divergences-non-goals)) does not count.

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-INGRESS-DEFAULT**: POST /swarm/init creates an ingress network named ingress

*Observed from:* api:solo, api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

/swarm/init` responds 200 on the node, an ingress network exists. Its name is
`ingress`.
