<a id="swarm-networking-known-divergences-non-goals"></a>

## Known divergences & non-goals

<a id="SWARM-OVL-V6-ADDRESSING"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVL-V6-ADDRESSING**: IPv6 addressing inside the overlay

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Not supported. With the default IPAM driver, `POST /networks/create` accepts an overlay
network with an IPv6 subnet, but the network is never allocated. An overlay network with
`EnableIPv6` set and without an IPv6 subnet is accepted, and the network's
attachments get IPv4 addresses only. Each attachment gets exactly one address. The service mesh
is IPv4-only.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-NOT-DATA-PATH"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-VXLAN-SOURCE-NOT-DATA-PATH**: Outer source address of VXLAN traffic

*Observed from:* underlay · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Not guaranteed. The outer source address is the address that the node's route to each peer
selects. It is meant to be the node's data-path address. When that route selects a different
address, peers drop all of the node's overlay traffic. Neither node's daemon log has an error
([moby/moby#53004](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/53004)).

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-ADDRESS**: Data-path address on Windows

*Observed from:* underlay · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* windows

*Needs:* [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY)

Not applied. A Windows node's tunnel endpoint is the address of its network adapter, whatever
`DataPathAddr` or the advertise address says.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-PORT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-WINDOWS-DATA-PATH-PORT**: Data-path port on Windows

*Observed from:* underlay · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* windows

*Needs:* [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY)

Not applied. Windows nodes do not use the cluster's data-path port. In a cluster with a
non-default data-path port, Windows nodes cannot exchange overlay traffic with Linux nodes.

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-IFACE-NAME-RESOLVED-ONCE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-IFACE-NAME-RESOLVED-ONCE**: Interface names as DataPathAddr or AdvertiseAddr

*Observed from:* underlay · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Resolved one time. `POST /swarm/init` and `POST /swarm/join` replace an
interface name with the interface's address when the request is made. The node keeps that
address after the interface's address changes. It also keeps it after the daemon restarts, even
when no interface on the node has that address
([Cluster & node configuration](#swarm-networking-cluster-node-configuration)).

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-MIXED-VERSIONS-ACCEPTED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-DATA-PATH-MIXED-VERSIONS-ACCEPTED**: Mixed IPv4 and IPv6 data-path addresses

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Not refused. A node can join a Swarm with a data-path address of a different IP version from the
data-path addresses of the other nodes. Overlay traffic between two nodes whose data-path
addresses have different IP versions fails. Only the daemon log of each node reports the failure
to program the other node as a peer ([Cluster & node configuration](#swarm-networking-cluster-node-configuration),
[*SWARM-FAILREP-PEER*](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-FAILREP-PEER)).

<a id="SWARM-OVL-ALLOCATION-FAILURE-UNREPORTED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVL-ALLOCATION-FAILURE-UNREPORTED**: Network allocation failures are not reported to the caller

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

`POST /networks/create` for an overlay network that cannot be allocated responds 201.
This occurs when a VNI in the network's `vxlanid_list` is in use, or when its address
pool is exhausted. It also occurs when its requested subnet overlaps the subnet of another Swarm
network. It also occurs when it has an IPv6 subnet under the default IPAM driver. Networks are
allocated asynchronously. When a network cannot be allocated, the failure appears in the leader
manager's log. Allocation is tried again later, for example after another network, service or
task is removed. Nothing tells the caller about the failure. `POST /services/create` for
a service on such a network also responds 201. The service's tasks never start, and nothing
tells the caller why. On a manager, `GET /networks/{id}` reports the network with an
empty `Driver` and `IPAM`, even when the request named them
([Overlay networks](#swarm-networking-overlay-networks), [Scale and exhaustion](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-scale-and-exhaustion)).

<a id="SWARM-OVL-STATUS-FULL-ID"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVL-STATUS-FULL-ID**: Network status by full ID on a manager

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Node-local. Take a manager that has a local attachment to an overlay network. On that manager,
`GET /networks/{id}` with the network's full ID reports only that node's own endpoints
in `Status.IPAM`. With the network's name or a partial ID, it reports the manager's
allocation for the whole network ([Overlay networks](#swarm-networking-overlay-networks)).

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-HTTP500-REFUSED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-HTTP500-REFUSED**: HTTP 500 for refused requests

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pinned by:* [NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-SWARM-START-FAILS](network-common.md#NET-API-CONNECT-MISSING-SWARM-START-FAILS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Each request below is refused on purpose, but the request responds 500. 500 is the status for a
fault in the daemon. The requests are: (1) `POST /swarm/init` with a data-path port
outside the accepted range. (2) `POST /swarm/init` with a `SubnetSize`
greater than 29, or with a `SubnetSize` less than the prefix length of one of its `DefaultAddrPool` prefixes, or of 0 with one of those prefixes longer than 24 bits. (3) `POST /swarm/init` and `POST
/swarm/join` with `live-restore` true. (4) `POST /swarm/init` and
`POST /swarm/join` with `firewall-backend` set to `nftables`, with
`iptables` true, and without `features.swarm-nftables`. (5)
`POST /containers/{id}/start` for a created or stopped container on a non-attachable
Swarm-scoped network, and `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to such a network for a running
container. (6) `POST /containers/{id}/start` for a created or stopped container that
publishes a port that a service publishes in ingress mode. (7) On a node in a Swarm,
`POST /containers/{id}/start` for a created or stopped container whose network was
deleted after the container was created, or never existed. For some other invalid `POST
/swarm/init` parameters, such as an invalid listen address, the request responds 400
([Cluster & node configuration](#swarm-networking-cluster-node-configuration),
[Swarm-scoped networks](#swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks), [Port allocation](swarm-traffic.md#swarm-traffic-port-allocation),
[Churn](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-churn)).

<a id="SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-ZERO-UNALLOCATED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-CLUSTER-SUBNET-SIZE-ZERO-UNALLOCATED**: SubnetSize of 0 at init

*Observed from:* api:solo · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Accepted. `POST /swarm/init` with `DefaultAddrPool` set, with no prefix longer than 24 bits, and a `SubnetSize` of 0 responds 200. The leader manager then cannot create its network
allocator. No Swarm-scoped network is allocated, the ingress network included. Only the leader
manager's log reports this, in an entry that contains `failed to create allocator`
([Cluster & node configuration](#swarm-networking-cluster-node-configuration)).

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-WORKER-OVERLAY-CREATE-ERROR"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-WORKER-OVERLAY-CREATE-ERROR**: Error for an overlay network created on a worker

*Observed from:* api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Rationale:* Why a change to SWARM-SCOPED-WORKER-OVERLAY-CREATE-ERROR should be deliberate ([RAT-SWARM-SCOPED-WORKER-OVERLAY-CREATE-ERROR](swarm-lifecycle.md#RAT-SWARM-SCOPED-WORKER-OVERLAY-CREATE-ERROR))

Misleading. On a worker, the error from `docker network create --driver overlay` says
`This node is not a swarm manager. Use "docker swarm init" or "docker swarm join" to
connect this node to swarm and try again.`. This error tells a node that is already in a Swarm
to join a Swarm ([Swarm-scoped networks](#swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks)).

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-ON-LEADER"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-ON-LEADER**: Network and IPAM plugins on the leader

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Required. A Swarm-scoped network whose driver or IPAM driver is a managed plugin can be created
and allocated only while the leader manager has the plugin. After leadership moves to a manager
without the plugin, the network still reports its allocation. But the tasks of services on it
stay in the `new` state that `GET /tasks` reports. Only the leader manager's log
reports the failure ([Swarm-scoped networks](#swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks)).

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-UNTAGGED-NAME"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-PLUGIN-UNTAGGED-NAME**: Plugin names without a tag

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Inconsistent. A managed plugin is found by its name without the tag when the request is checked,
but its driver is registered under the full name. Thus `POST /networks/create` with a
network driver named without the tag responds 500. An IPAM driver named without the tag is
accepted, but the network is never allocated ([Swarm-scoped networks](#swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks)).

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-ONLY-ONE-NODE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-ONLY-ONE-NODE**: Config-only networks for Swarm-scoped networks

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Checked on one node. `POST /networks/create` for a Swarm-scoped network with
`ConfigFrom` responds 201 only when the config-only network exists on the manager
that handles the request. Each node that runs a task on the network uses its own config-only
network of that name. Thus a manager that does not run tasks needs the config-only network only
to allow the request. Task placement does not take into account which nodes have the config-only
network. A task can be placed on a node that does not have it. That task is then rejected. On
such a node, the attachment of a standalone container to the network fails after 20 seconds
([Swarm-scoped networks](#swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks)).

<a id="SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-PARTLY-SUPPORTED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-INGRESS-LABEL-PARTLY-SUPPORTED**: Ingress networks without Ingress

*Observed from:* client · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Partly supported. Older daemons created the ingress network as an overlay network named
`ingress` with the label `com.docker.swarm.internal`, without
`Ingress`. `POST /networks/create` still accepts this form, and the network
is treated as an ingress network. But a node sets up the routing mesh for it only while the node
has a local attachment to it. A published port is not reachable at the address of any other
node. When the network is deleted, the nodes keep their copies until the daemon restarts. A new
ingress network then fails on those nodes when its subnet overlaps. The checks that
`POST /networks/create` makes for `Ingress` do not apply to this form. Such a
network can be `Attachable`. It can also be created while another ingress network
exists, and it is then never allocated ([The ingress network](#swarm-networking-the-ingress-network)).

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-NAME-COLLISION-LOCAL**: Local and Swarm-scoped networks with the same name

*Observed from:* api:wkr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Not prevented on every node. A node can have a network that is not Swarm-scoped and that has the
name of a Swarm-scoped network. A worker can create such a network, and a worker that has one
can become a manager. `POST /networks/create` refuses the name only on the manager that
handles the request ([Swarm-scoped networks](#swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks)). On a manager with
both networks, a request that names the network by name is ambiguous. On any node with both
networks, the Swarm-scoped network is not usable. Its tasks are rejected there. A standalone
container that names it by its ID cannot attach to it. One that names it by its name is attached
to the other network.

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-OVERLAY-UNUSABLE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-CONFIG-FROM-OVERLAY-UNUSABLE**: --config-from on overlay networks

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Not usable. `POST /networks/create` for an overlay network with `ConfigFrom`
responds 201 only if the config-only network exists on the manager that handles the request. It
responds 404 otherwise. Every attachment to the network then fails. The tasks of a service fail
with `user-specified configurations are not supported if the network depends on a
configuration network`. `docker run` exits non-zero after 20 seconds and prints an error
that contains `attaching to network failed, make sure your network options are
correct and check manager logs: context deadline exceeded`
([Swarm-scoped networks](#swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks)).

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-FAILURE-TIMEOUT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-ATTACH-FAILURE-TIMEOUT**: Attachment failures for standalone containers time out

*Observed from:* api:active · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

If the attachment of a standalone container to an attachable network fails, `POST
/containers/{id}/start` waits 20 seconds. It then responds 500 with `attaching to
network failed, make sure your network options are correct and check manager logs: context
deadline exceeded`. This occurs in seven cases: (1) The network is `encrypted`, and the
host's kernel does not offer the XFRM netlink interface. (2) The network is an overlay network
created with `ConfigFrom`. (3) The network is deleted after the start has found it,
but before the attachment task is created. (4) The container's static address is in use or is
outside the network's subnets. (5) The network is not allocated. (6) The container's node has
availability `drain` or `pause`. (7) The network is a Swarm-scoped network of a node-local
driver created with `ConfigFrom`, and the container's node does not have the
config-only network that `ConfigFrom` names. `POST /networks/{id}/connect`
for a running container also waits 20 seconds in this case, and then responds 500 with the same
message. In cases 1, 2 and 7, the reason appears in the attachment task only while the start
waits. During that time, `GET /tasks` with the `runtime=attachment` filter
lists the task as rejected. Then the task is deleted before the request responds. After that,
the reason is only in the node's daemon log. In case 3, the attachment task is deleted, and no
manager's daemon log reports the failure. In cases 4 and 5, the attachment task stays in the
`new` state until it is deleted. `GET /tasks` reports that state. The reason then
appears only in the leader manager's log, in an entry that contains `task allocation
failure`. In case 6, the attachment task stays in the `pending` state until it is deleted.
`GET /tasks` reports that state ([Swarm-scoped networks](#swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks),
[Overlay networks](#swarm-networking-overlay-networks), [Encryption](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-encryption),
[Churn](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-churn), [Scale and exhaustion](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-scale-and-exhaustion)).

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-V6-ONLY"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-V6-ONLY**: IPv6-only Swarm-scoped networks of node-local drivers

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Rationale:* Why a change to SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-V6-ONLY should be deliberate ([RAT-SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-V6-ONLY](swarm-lifecycle.md#RAT-SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-V6-ONLY))

Refused. `POST /networks/create` for any Swarm-scoped network with
`EnableIPv4` false responds 400 with `IPv4 cannot be disabled in a Swarm
scoped network`. This holds whatever the network's driver is. Only `overlay` needs the
refusal ([Swarm-scoped networks](#swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks),
[Overlay networks](#swarm-networking-overlay-networks)).

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-IPAM-OPTIONS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-NODE-LOCAL-IPAM-OPTIONS**: Subnets and options on Swarm-scoped networks of node-local drivers

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Ignored. `POST /networks/create` accepts a valid `IPAM.Config` and
`Options` for a Swarm-scoped network of a node-local driver, but they are not kept.
Each node creates the network from its own default address pools and the driver's defaults. A
`ConfigFrom` that names a config-only network configures such a network on each node
([Swarm-scoped networks](#swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks)).

<a id="SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES-IGNORED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVL-AUXILIARY-ADDRESSES-IGNORED**: Auxiliary addresses on overlay networks

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Ignored. `POST /networks/create` accepts `AuxiliaryAddresses` in the
`IPAM.Config` of an overlay network, but they are not kept. These addresses are not
reserved, and tasks and VIPs can get them ([Overlay networks](#swarm-networking-overlay-networks)).

<a id="SWARM-OVL-MTU-UNCHECKED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-OVL-MTU-UNCHECKED**: mtu on Swarm networks is not checked at create

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Accepted. `POST /networks/create` with any value of
`com.docker.network.driver.mtu` responds 201. If the value is not a non-negative
integer, a Linux node rejects all tasks on the network that are assigned to that node. Their
errors contain `failed to parse` or `invalid MTU value`. If the kernel
cannot create the network's interfaces with the value, every such task fails at start. Windows
nodes ignore the option ([Overlay networks](#swarm-networking-overlay-networks)).

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-IFACE-NAME-OPTION-UNCHECKED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-IFACE-NAME-OPTION-UNCHECKED**: ifname is not checked before a task starts

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Accepted. `POST /services/create` and `POST /services/{id}/update` accept any
interface name in the driver options of a network attachment. Every task with an interface name
that the OS refuses fails at start. Under the default restart policy, such a task is replaced
indefinitely ([Swarm-scoped networks](#swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks)).

<a id="SWARM-SCOPED-HOST-NETWORK-COMBINED-ACCEPTED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) SWARM-SCOPED-HOST-NETWORK-COMBINED-ACCEPTED**: Services on the host network with other networks

*Observed from:* api:mgr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN)

Accepted. `POST /services/create` for a service attached to the `host` network
and to an overlay network responds 201. `POST /services/create` for a service on
`host` that publishes a port in ingress mode also responds 201. Every task of such a
service fails at start. Under the default restart policy, such a task is replaced indefinitely
([Swarm-scoped networks](#swarm-networking-swarm-scoped-networks)).

<a id="swarm-networking-deliberately-not-asserted"></a>

## Deliberately not asserted

These items are incidental to the implementation. A change to any of them does not break any
expectation.

- The counters of Moby's own rules.
- Precedence over an operator's rule that the operator inserts at the top of the filter table's
  `INPUT` chain after an `encrypted` network is programmed. Such a rule can
  accept cleartext VXLAN for the network's VNI ([iptables](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-iptables)).
- The content of Moby's own chains and tables, and their names other than `DOCKER-USER`,
  except where [Cross-generation cleanup](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-cross-generation-cleanup) pins them for cleanup and
  [Rule content](bridge-networking.md#bridge-networking-rule-content) pins the bridge driver's rules. The content includes
  individual match/target lines and their order in a chain. A backend change replaces exactly these
  rules. A contract asserts their effect on packets, and never the content.
- Which packet-filtering technology is in use, beyond what the
  [Firewall anchors & host integration](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-firewall-anchors-host-integration) expectations about anchors and cleanup
  assert for each backend.
- The existence, name or topology of internal sandboxes (per-network load-balancer sandbox, ingress
  sandbox), network-namespace paths, and generated `veth` / bridge / VXLAN interface
  names. One exception is the name `ingress-sbox` in `Containers` of `GET
  /networks/docker_gwbridge`, which [Network API](network-common.md#network-common-network-api) pins. Another exception is a
  node's load-balancer endpoint on a network. `GET /networks/{id}` on that node lists this
  endpoint. [Overlay networks](#swarm-networking-overlay-networks) asserts where its address falls, and
  [Load balancing (east-west VIP)](swarm-traffic.md#swarm-traffic-load-balancing-east-west-vip) asserts that a task observes it as the source
  address in NAT mode. The key and the name of this endpoint are not asserted.
  [Daemon restart](network-common.md#network-common-daemon-restart) asserts that the namespaces of these sandboxes are removed
  after a kill and restart.
- The load-balancer implementation and its scheduler, beyond the distribution property in
  [Distribution](swarm-traffic.md#swarm-traffic-distribution).
- Internal refcounting, gossip timers, and reap and rejoin intervals. The surface for these is the
  convergence bounds in [Convergence](swarm-lifecycle.md#swarm-lifecycle-convergence).
- The order in which the daemon allocates subnets from an address pool, addresses within a subnet,
  published ports from the auto-assignment range, and VNIs to networks created without
  `vxlanid_list`.
- The value of `LocalLBIndex`. `docker network inspect --verbose` shows this value,
  but the value is an internal firewall mark.
- The host-port reservation mechanics behind [Port allocation](swarm-traffic.md#swarm-traffic-port-allocation).
- Whether Windows nodes can use a VNI below 4096.
